questions.question: Which of the following organ systems jointly coordinate and integrate all the activities of the body organs so that they function in a synchronised fashion?
questions.explanation: The neural system and endocrine system work together to coordinate and integrate all the activities of the body's organs in a synchronized manner. The neural system provides fast and precise point-to-point coordination through nerve impulses, while the endocrine system provides chemical integration via hormones, ensuring long-term regulation and homeostasis.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से अंग तंत्र संयुक्त रूप से शरीर के सभी अंगों की गतिविधियों का समन्वय और एकीकरण करते हैं ताकि वे एक समकालिक तरीके से कार्य करें?

questions.question: The functions of the organs/organ systems in our body must be coordinated to maintain
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable internal environment through the coordination of organ systems.

hi.question: हमारे शरीर में अंगों/अंग प्रणालियों के कार्यों को बनाए रखने के लिए समन्वित किया जाना चाहिए

questions.question: The process through which two or more organs interact and complement the functions of one another is called
questions.explanation: Coordination is the process where two or more organs interact to function harmoniously.

hi.question: दो या अधिक अंगों के परस्पर क्रिया करने और एक दूसरे के कार्यों को पूरक करने की प्रक्रिया को कहा जाता है:

questions.question: The system responsible for providing an organised network of point to point connections for a quick coordination is called
questions.explanation: The neural system is responsible for providing an organized network of point-to-point connections, enabling quick coordination of body functions. It achieves this through nerve impulses, which are transmitted rapidly across neurons to ensure immediate responses to stimuli.

hi.question: त्वरित समन्वय के लिए बिंदु-दर-बिंदु संयोजन का एक संगठित नेटवर्क प्रदान करने के लिए जिम्मेदार तंत्र को कहा जाता है-

questions.question: The neural system is better organised in ____A____ where a brain is present along with a number of ____B____and ____C____.
options: Insect, ganglia and neural tissues, respectively
Hydra, neural tissues and ganglia, respectively
questions.explanation: Insects have a better-organized neural system with a brain, ganglia, and neural tissues. Hydra lacks a brain but has a nerve net instead. Vertebrates have a brain but do not rely on ganglia for coordination.

hi.question: तंत्रिका तंत्र A में बेहतर रूप से व्यवस्थित होता है जहाँ एक मस्तिष्क B और C की संख्या के साथ मौजूद होता है।

questions.question: Which of the following system provides the fastest means of communication within the body?
questions.explanation: The nervous system provides the fastest means of communication via electrical impulses.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी प्रणाली शरीर के भीतर संचार का सबसे तेज़ साधन प्रदान करती है?

questions.question: Endocrine system provides chemical integration through:
questions.explanation: (1) The endocrine system regulates body functions through hormones, which act as chemical messengers. [New NCERT Class 11th Page no. 239]

hi.question: अंतःस्रावी तंत्र रासायनिक एकीकरण प्रदान करता है:

questions.question: The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialised cells called
questions.explanation: The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialized cells called neurons. These cells are responsible for detecting, receiving, and transmitting different kinds of stimuli. Neurons are the structural and functional units of the nervous system.

hi.question: सभी जन्तुओं का तंत्रिका तंत्र अत्यधिक विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं से मिलकर बना होता है, जो कहलाती है:
hi.explanation: सभी जानवरों का तंत्रिका तंत्र अत्यधिक विशिष्ट कोशिकाओं से बना होता है जिन्हें न्यूरॉन्स कहा जाता है। ये कोशिकाएँ विभिन्न प्रकार की उत्तेजनाओं का पता लगाने, उन्हें प्राप्त करने और संचारित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार होती हैं। न्यूरॉन्स तंत्रिका तंत्र की संरचनात्मक और कार्यात्मक इकाइयाँ हैं।

questions.question: Neurons are specialised cells for
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialized cells that are responsible for the conduction of nerve impulses. They receive, process, and transmit information through electrical and chemical signals, facilitating communication between different parts of the body.

hi.question: न्यूरॉन विशिष्ट कोशिकाएँ हैं-
options: तंत्रिका आवेगों के चालन के लिए

questions.question: Neurons can
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialized cells that detect, receive, and transmit stimuli in the form of electrical and chemical signals. They play a crucial role in the neural system by ensuring rapid communication between different parts of the body.

hi.question: न्यूरॉन्स का कार्य हैं-

questions.question: Basic functions of neural system is/are
options: Receiving sensory input from internal and external environment by nerves
questions.explanation: The neural system performs the following basic functions: Receiving sensory input from both the internal and external environment through nerves. Processing the input information in the central nervous system (CNS), primarily in the brain and spinal cord. Responding to stimuli by transmitting nerve impulses to effector organs such as muscles and glands for appropriate actions. Thus, all the given options are correct.

hi.question: तंत्रिका तंत्र के मूल कार्य हैं-
options: तंत्रिकाओं द्वारा आंतरिक और बाहरी वातावरण से संवेदी इनपुट प्राप्त करना
hi.explanation: तंत्रिका तंत्र निम्नलिखित मूल कार्य करता है: तंत्रिकाओं के माध्यम से आंतरिक और बाह्य दोनों पर्यावरण से संवेदी निवेश प्राप्त करना। केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) में, मुख्य रूप से मस्तिष्क और मेरुरज्जु में निवेशित सूचनाओं का प्रसंस्करण करना। उचित क्रियाओं के लिए पेशियों तथा ग्रंथियों जैसे कार्यकर अंगों तक तंत्रिका आवेगों को संचारित करके उद्दीपनों के प्रति अनुक्रिया करना। अतः, दिए गए सभी विकल्प सही हैं।

questions.question: Which of the following have a more developed neural system?
questions.explanation: The complexity of the neural system increases in the following order: Lower invertebrates (e.g., Hydra) have a simple nerve net without a central nervous system. Insects have a more organized neural system, including a brain and ganglia. Vertebrates have the most developed neural system, consisting of a highly specialized brain, spinal cord, and a complex network of nerves for rapid communication and coordination. Thus, vertebrates possess the most advanced neural system.

hi.question: निम्नलिखित में से किसमें अधिक विकसित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है?
hi.explanation: तंत्रिका तंत्र की जटिलता निम्नलिखित क्रम में बढ़ती है: निम्न अकशेरुकियों (जैसे, हाइड्रा) में केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र के बिना एक सरल तंत्रिका जाल होता है। कीटों में अधिक संगठित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है, जिसमें मस्तिष्क और गुच्छिकाएँ शामिल होती हैं। कशेरुकियों में सबसे विकसित तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है, जिसमें तीव्र संचार और समन्वय के लिए एक अत्यधिक विशिष्टीकृत मस्तिष्क, मेरुरज्जु और तंत्रिकाओं का एक जटिल जाल होता है। अतः, कशेरुकियों में सबसे उन्नत तंत्रिका तंत्र होता है।

questions.question: The human neural system is divided into
options: Three parts- CNS, PNS and ANS
Three parts- Forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain
questions.explanation: The human neural system is divided into two main parts: Central Nervous System (CNS) - Consists of the brain and spinal cord, responsible for processing and controlling information. Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) - Comprises all the nerves that connect the CNS to different parts of the body. It includes: Somatic Nervous System (voluntary control) Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) (involuntary control) Thus, the neural system is primarily divided into CNS and PNS, making option A correct.

hi.question: मानव तंत्रिका तंत्र को विभाजित किया गया है-
options: दो भागों में- CNS और PNS
दो भागों में- CNS और ANS
तीन भागों में- CNS, PNS और ANS
तीन भागों में- अग्रमस्तिष्क, मध्यमस्तिष्क और पश्चमस्तिष्क
hi.explanation: मानव तंत्रिका तंत्र दो मुख्य भागों में विभाजित है: केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) - इसमें मस्तिष्क और मेरुरज्जु शामिल हैं, जो सूचनाओं के प्रसंस्करण और नियंत्रण के लिए उत्तरदायी है। परिधीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (PNS) - इसमें वे सभी तंत्रिकाएँ शामिल हैं जो CNS को शरीर के विभिन्न भागों से जोड़ती हैं। इसमें शामिल हैं: कायिक तंत्रिका तंत्र (ऐच्छिक नियंत्रण) स्वायत्त तंत्रिका तंत्र (ANS) (अनैच्छिक नियंत्रण) अतः, तंत्रिका तंत्र मुख्य रूप से CNS और PNS में विभाजित है, जिससे विकल्प A सही है।

questions.question: Afferent nerve fibres carry impulses from
questions.explanation: Afferent nerve fibers are responsible for carrying sensory impulses from receptors (sensory organs) to the central nervous system (CNS). These impulses provide information about external and internal stimuli to the brain or spinal cord for processing. In contrast, efferent nerve fibers carry motor commands from the CNS to effectors (muscles and glands).

hi.question: अभिवाही तंत्रिका तंतु आवेगों को वहन करते हैं।
options: प्रभावी अंग से ग्राही के लिये
hi.explanation: अभिवाही तंत्रिका तंतु रिसेप्टर्स (संवेदी अंगों) से केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (सीएनएस) तक संवेदी आवेगों को ले जाने के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं। ये आवेग मस्तिष्क या रीढ़ की हड्डी को प्रसंस्करण के लिए बाहरी और आंतरिक उत्तेजनाओं के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करते हैं। इसके विपरीत, अपवाही तंत्रिका तंतु सीएनएस से प्रभावकों (मांसपेशियों और ग्रंथियों) तक मोटर कमांड ले जाते हैं।

questions.question: Visceral nervous system is the part of
questions.explanation: The visceral nervous system is a part of the peripheral nervous system (PNS). It consists of nerves, fibres, ganglia and plexuses that transmit impulses between the central nervous system (CNS) and visceral organs (such as the heart, lungs, intestines, etc.). It plays a crucial role in autonomic functions like digestion, respiration and circulation.

hi.question: अंतरंग तंत्रिका तंत्र निम्न का भाग है:
hi.explanation: आंत संबंधी तंत्रिका तंत्र परिधीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (PNS) का एक हिस्सा है। इसमें तंत्रिकाएँ, तंतु, गैन्ग्लिया और प्लेक्सस होते हैं जो केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) और आंत संबंधी अंगों (जैसे हृदय, फेफड़े, आंत, आदि) के बीच आवेगों को संचारित करते हैं। यह पाचन, श्वसन और परिसंचरण जैसे स्वायत्त कार्यों में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

questions.question: Multipolar neurons are found in the
questions.explanation: Multipolar neurons have one axon and two or more dendrites and are the most common type of neurons in the human body. They are primarily found in the cerebral cortex, where they play a crucial role in higher-order brain functions such as cognition, motor control, and sensory processing. Retina of the eye (A) contains bipolar neurons (one axon and one dendrite). Embryonic stage (C) is associated with unipolar neurons, not multipolar neurons. None of the above (D) is incorrect as multipolar neurons are present in the cerebral cortex.

hi.question: बहुध्रुवीय न्यूरॉन पाए जाते हैं-

questions.question: Unmyelinated nerve fibres that do not form a myelin sheath around the axon are commonly found in _____ A _____and the _____B_____ neural systems. Fill in the blanks ( {A} and {B} ) with correct option.
questions.explanation: Unmyelinated nerve fibers are commonly found in the autonomous nervous system (ANS) and the somatic neural system. The ANS controls involuntary functions and includes sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions, where many neurons are unmyelinated. The somatic neural system contains both myelinated and unmyelinated fibers that control voluntary muscle movements.

hi.question: अनाच्चादी तंत्रिका तंतु जो तंत्रिकाक्ष के चारों ओर एक माइलिन आच्छद नहीं बनाते हैं, आमतौर पर .......... A .......... और .......... B .......... तंत्रिका तंत्र में पाए जाते हैं।रिक्त स्थान (A और B) को सही विकल्प से भरें।

questions.question: In resting stage, the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to __________A_________ ions and nearly impermeable to_________B_________. Fill in the blanks ( {A} and {B} ) with correct option
questions.explanation: During the resting stage of a neuron: The axonal membrane is more permeable to potassium (K⁺) ions, allowing them to move freely. The membrane is nearly impermeable to sodium (Na⁺) ions, preventing their free movement. This selective permeability is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump, which actively transports 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in, helping maintain the resting membrane potential (-70 mV).

questions.question: When the neuron is resting, the axonal membrane is................ to negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm
questions.explanation: During the resting stage, the axonal membrane is impermeable to negatively charged proteins present inside the axoplasm. These proteins contribute to the negative charge inside the neuron, helping establish the resting membrane potential (-70 mV). Additionally: The membrane is selectively permeable to K⁺ (potassium) ions, allowing them to move out. It is nearly impermeable to Na⁺ (sodium) ions, preventing their inward movement. The sodium-potassium pump actively maintains the resting potential by exchanging 3 Na⁺ out for 2 K⁺ in.

hi.question: जब न्यूरॉन विश्राम अवस्था में होता है, तो तंत्रिकाक्ष झिल्ली अक्षद्रव्य में मौजूद ऋणात्मक रूप से आवेशित प्रोटीनों के लिए ................. होती है

questions.question: The electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane when concentration of {K}^{+} is high inside the axon and low outside, it is known as
questions.explanation: During the resting state of a neuron, the concentration of K⁺ (potassium) ions is high inside the axon and low outside, while Na⁺ (sodium) ions are high outside and low inside. This results in an electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane, known as the resting potential (~ -70mV). The sodium-potassium pump helps maintain this potential by actively transporting 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in. Other options: Action potential (A) occurs when there is a rapid change in membrane potential due to Na⁺ influx. Refractory potential (C) refers to the period after an action potential when the neuron cannot generate another impulse immediately. All of the above (D) is incorrect as only resting potential fits the given condition.

hi.question: जब {K}^{+} की सांद्रता तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंदर अधिक और बाहर कम होती है, तो प्लाज्मा झिल्ली के पार विद्युत विभव अंतर को कहा जाता है-

questions.question: A wave of action potential is termed as
questions.explanation: A wave of action potential propagating along the neuron is known as a nerve impulse. This impulse is generated due to the depolarization and repolarization of the neuron membrane, allowing electrical signals to be transmitted. Sensory impulse (A) refers to signals transmitted by sensory neurons to the central nervous system. Activation impulse (C) is not a standard term in neurophysiology. Motor impulse (D) refers to signals carried by motor neurons to muscles or glands, but the general term for an action potential wave is nerve impulse.

hi.question: क्रियात्मक विभव की एक तरंग को कहा जाता है

questions.question: Maintenance of the ionic gradients across the resting membrane is done by
questions.explanation: The ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump), which actively transports: 3 Na⁺ ions out of the neuron 2 K⁺ ions in This process requires ATP and is an example of active transport of ions to maintain the resting membrane potential (-70mV). Passive transport of ions (B) does not require energy and occurs through diffusion, but the maintenance of gradients requires active transport. Active/passive transport of neurotransmitters (C & D) are involved in synaptic transmission, not in maintaining resting potential.

hi.question: विश्राम झिल्ली के पार आयनिक प्रवणताओं का रखरखाव किसके द्वारा किया जाता है?

questions.question: For the maintenance of ionic gradients across the resting membrane, the sodium-potassium pump transports
questions.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump) is responsible for maintaining the resting membrane potential by actively transporting: 3 Na⁺ (sodium) ions out of the neuron 2 K⁺ (potassium) ions into the neuron This process: Requires ATP (active transport) Helps in maintaining the ionic gradient Keeps the inside of the neuron negatively charged compared to the outside Other options are incorrect because they do not reflect the correct direction and ratio of ion transport.

hi.question: विश्राम झिल्ली के पार आयनिक प्रवणताओं के रखरखाव के लिए, सोडियम-पोटेशियम पंप परिवहन करता है-
options: 3Na+ बाहर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका में।
2Na+ बाहर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका में।
3Na+ अंदर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका से बाहर।
2Na+ अंदर की ओर 2 K+ कोशिका से बाहर

questions.question: In the resting stage of a neuron, concentration gradient generates due to
options: High concentration of {K}^{+} and low concentration of {Na}^{+} inside the axon
High concentration of {Na}^{+} and low concentration of {K}^{+} inside the axon
Low concentration of {Na}^{+} outside the axon
High concentration of {K}^{+} outside the axon
questions.explanation: During the resting stage of a neuron, the concentration gradient is maintained by the sodium-potassium pump (Na⁺/K⁺ pump), which actively transports: 3 Na⁺ out of the neuron 2 K⁺ in to the neuron As a result: Inside the axon: High K⁺, Low Na⁺ Outside the axon: High Na⁺, Low K⁺ This ionic gradient helps maintain the resting membrane potential (-70 mV), making the inside of the neuron negatively charged compared to the outside.

questions.question: During the transmission of nerve impulse through a nerve fibre, the potential on the inner side of the plasma membrane has ............... type of electric charge
options: First +ve then -ve and continue to be -ve
First +ve then -ve and again back to +ve
First -ve then +ve and again back to -ve
questions.explanation: During the transmission of a nerve impulse, the electric charge on the inner side of the plasma membrane undergoes the following changes: Resting potential (-ve inside): The inner side of the neuron membrane is negatively charged, and the outer side is positively charged due to the high concentration of K⁺ inside and Na⁺ outside. Depolarization (+ve inside): When an action potential is generated, Na⁺ ions rush into the neuron, making the inner side positively charged and the outer side negative. Repolarization (-ve inside again): K⁺ ions move out, restoring the negative charge inside the neuron and the positive charge outside. Thus, the sequence of changes is:Negative (-ve) → Positive (+ve) → Negative (-ve) again, which matches option (D).

questions.question: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: {K}^{+} ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid.
{Na}^{+} ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid.
{K}^{+} ions from extracellular fluid to intra cellular fluid.
{Na}^{+} ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid.
questions.explanation: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, an action potential is generated due to the influx of Na⁺ ions into the neuron. At resting potential (-70 mV): The neuron is more negative inside due to a high concentration of K⁺ inside and Na⁺ outside. During depolarization (Action potential): Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open, allowing Na⁺ ions to rush into the intracellular fluid. This makes the inside of the neuron positively charged compared to the outside. Repolarization: K⁺ channels open, and K⁺ moves out, restoring the negative charge inside the neuron. Thus, the movement of Na⁺ ions from extracellular to intracellular fluid is responsible for generating the action potential.

questions.question: "Jumping of the action potential" at the nodes of Ranvier is known as:
questions.explanation: Saltatory conduction refers to the jumping of action potentials between nodes of Ranvier in myelinated nerve fibers, speeding up impulse transmission. Other options are incorrect: Neurotransmission (B) → General term for signal transfer between neurons. Recovery phase (C) & Active phase (D) → Refer to different stages of the action potential, not jumping conduction.

questions.question: The ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the
questions.explanation: The ionic gradient across the resting membrane is primarily maintained by the sodium-potassium pump. This pump actively transports sodium ions out of the cell and potassium ions into the cell, creating and maintaining the concentration differences across the membrane.

questions.question: On application of a stimulus on the axonal membrane
options: there is a rapid influx of {K}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid efflux of {Na}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid influx of {Na}^{+} at that site.
there is a rapid efflux of {K}^{+} at that site.
questions.explanation: When a stimulus is applied to the axonal membrane, it causes depolarization by opening voltage-gated Na⁺ channels, leading to: Rapid influx of Na⁺ ions into the neuron. The inside of the membrane becomes positively charged compared to the outside. This change in charge triggers an action potential, allowing the nerve impulse to propagate. Efflux of Na⁺ (Option B) does not occur during depolarization. Influx or efflux of K⁺ (Options A & D) happens during repolarization, not at the start of the action potential.
